# duploai_plan_kms_key (Resource)

Registers an existing, customer-managed KMS key against a duploai_plan, making it selectable by every resource group in the environments that plan is attached to. Resources such as duploai_node_group, duploai_s3_bucket and duploai_rds_instance reference it through their own kms_key_id attribute; the backend resolves that value against the resource group's own registry first, then the plan-level registry. Register a key here rather than per resource group when one key should serve a whole environment. Registration does not grant any permissions on the key — its own key policy must already trust the account and role that will use it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Register an existing customer-managed KMS key against a plan, so every
# resource group in the environments that plan is attached to can encrypt with
# it. Register at the plan level for one key serving a whole environment; use
# duploai_resource_group_kms_key when the key belongs to a single group.
#
# The key's own key policy must already trust this account/role — registering it
# here does not modify the policy.
#
# All three of key_name, key_id and key_arn are required by the API, and each
# must be unique within the plan.
resource "duploai_plan_kms_key" "cmek" {
  workspace_id = "<workspace-id>"
  plan_id      = duploai_plan.basic.plan_id

  key_name = "environment-cmek"
  key_id   = "1234abcd-12ab-34cd-56ef-1234567890ab"
  key_arn  = "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/1234abcd-12ab-34cd-56ef-1234567890ab"
}

# Consuming resources resolve either form against the registry. Referencing the
# ARN keeps the dependency explicit, so Terraform registers the key first.
resource "duploai_node_group" "encrypted" {
  workspace_id      = "<workspace-id>"
  name              = "encrypted-nodes"
  environment_id    = "<environment-id>"
  resource_group_id = "<resource-group-id>"
  scope_ids         = ["<scope-id>"]

  instance_types = ["t3.large"]
  ami_type       = "AL2023_x86_64_STANDARD"
  min_size       = 1
  max_size       = 2
  desired_size   = 1

  kms_key_id = duploai_plan_kms_key.cmek.key_arn
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key_arn` (String) ARN of the existing customer-managed KMS key, e.g. arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/1234abcd-12ab-34cd-56ef-1234567890ab. Required, and must be unique within the plan. Prefer wiring this value into a consuming resource's kms_key_id: it is unambiguous across accounts and regions, and it is what the backend stores and hands to the cloud.
- `key_id` (String) Raw AWS KMS key ID, e.g. 1234abcd-12ab-34cd-56ef-1234567890ab. Required by the API even though it also appears inside key_arn, and must be unique within the plan. Consuming resources may pass either this or key_arn as their kms_key_id.
- `key_name` (String) Friendly label for this registration. Required by the API, and must be unique within the plan (compared case-insensitively).
- `plan_id` (String) ID of the duploai_plan to register this key against. The plan must belong to workspace_id.
- `workspace_id` (String) ID of the workspace that owns the parent plan.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite resource identifier (workspace_id/id).
- `key_entry_id` (String) This registration's own backend record ID, distinct from key_id (the AWS KMS key's ID). The API deletes a registration by this value.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing plan-level KMS key registration.
#  - WORKSPACE_ID is the ID of the workspace (e.g. 00000000000000000000aaaa)
#  - PLAN_ID is the plan's backend record ID (e.g. 00000000000000000000bbbb)
#  - KEY_ENTRY_ID is this registration's own backend record ID, not the AWS KMS key ID (e.g. 000000000000000000000000000cccc1)
terraform import duploai_plan_kms_key.cmek WORKSPACE_ID/PLAN_ID/KEY_ENTRY_ID
# Example:
# terraform import duploai_plan_kms_key.cmek 00000000000000000000aaaa/00000000000000000000bbbb/000000000000000000000000000cccc1
```
